thread:
mike: hey all — quick sync: we need a clear policy for request/response logging for hosted API. specifically: sampling rates, what we redact, and how this shows up in the console dashboards. thinking we should standardize defaults + per-customer overrides. thoughts?
anna: +1 on defaults. compliance wants minimal default retention and aggressive PII redaction. can we enumerate what counts as PII for our purposes? names, emails, phone numbers, credit cards, SSNs, auth tokens, and any long form free-text that contains those.
sarah: for observability we also need to surface sampling metadata (why a request was kept or dropped) and a per-model token/sample cost estimate. dashboard should show sample_rate, selective fields removed, and hashed customer_id.
mike: good — two followups: 1) sampling determinism — should we do deterministic sampling by customer_id/request_id so we can replay distributions? 2) redaction: redact at ingestion or store raw encrypted and redact at read?
kevin: ingestion-time redaction is simpler and avoids secrets storage, but loses ability to re-evaluate later if redaction rules improve. storing encrypted raw requires KMS + access audit, increases compliance burden. my leaning: default to ingestion-time redaction with an opt-in enterprise flag to store encrypted raw for customers that need it.
anna: that matches compliance: we can allow encrypted retention under strict contract + HSM/KMS, with explicit TTLs and SOC2 audit trail. also must support subject access requests: ability to delete or export user data.
sarah: sampling approach: two tiers. global default sample_rate=0.01 (1%) for user-visible text requests, and higher for errors and slow responses (100% for 5xx or latency>1s). also allow per-customer sampling overrides and deterministic sampler seeded by customer_id so slices are stable. we should log sampler_decision and sampler_seed in telemetry.
mike: can we add a small config example for the console? for product folks.
sarah: sure — single-line config example: 
```
logging:
  sample_rate: 0.01
  deterministic_by: customer_id
  error_sample_rate: 1.0    # always keep errors
  redact_level: semantic   # options: none, token, semantic
  retention_days: 30
```
kevin: redaction levels: token = strip tokens matching regex for emails/cc/etc; semantic = run an NER model to identify entities and redact spans (better recall but heavier CPU). we should default to token for hosted, semantic optional for enterprise.
anna: require that Authorization, Cookie, and private headers are always stripped server-side regardless of redact_level. also mask top-level JSON keys named "email", "phone", "ssn", "credit_card" even if token regex misses them.
compliance-bot: reminder: GDPR controllers need Data Processing Agreement + right-to-be-forgotten flows. Document: https://intranet.redwood/proc/policy/logging-redaction (stub).
mike: UX for rollouts: product wants an on/off toggle per-customer in console with a preview modal showing examples (redacted vs raw) — raw only if customer has encrypted-storage flag. we need backend API: POST /v1/customers/{id}/logging-config
kevin: API shape is fine. recommend conservative default that blocks raw preview unless user has admin role + approved contract. also add an audit event for any raw access.
sarah: for dashboards, add these widgets: sample rate heatmap over time, percent of requests redacted, top redacted tokens, errors preserved by sampling. small table for recent sampled traces with sampler_decision and redaction_summary.
mike: operational concerns: sampling can bias metrics. we need docs explaining how to compute QPS, cost, and error rates from sampled logs (weighted by 1/sample_rate or use reservoir sampling flags).
anna: agree — include compliance note: exports must state what was redacted and why (e.g., token-rule X matched). also keep an exportable manifest for subject requests.
kevin: implementation note: use a gate in the API filter chain: 1) header strip, 2) compute sampler decision, 3) if keep -> run redaction pipeline -> persist telemetry and logs. keep pipeline idempotent.
mike: sounds like action items: anna draft compliance appendix, kevin prototype ingestion pipeline + KMS checks, sarah mock console widgets + example config, i'll draft the customer-facing guidance page. can we aim for a PR by end of week?
sarah: I can mock up widgets by Thursday. :thumbsup:
kevin: will start prototyping ingestion filter, aim for Friday.
anna: I'll draft the compliance appendix and list mandatory headers & fields by Thursday.
compliance-bot: note: flagged for review by legal once initial draft is ready.
mike: perfect — thanks team. ping me on-thread for sync or if you need product clarifications. :rocket:
